info.title: conductord
info.summary: The daemon of the control host. It reconciles every instance of the config file against what runs at its placement, opens and closes each instance's box, resolves the secrets the config names, records who operates each instance and the tokens they contribute, writes the config on an accepted change, and serves the global API.
info.description:
The HTTP surface of `conductord`, one of the components of `conductor` v1.

Every path here is one semantic command, so the method is always POST and the path is the command's wire name under its domain's: a command is not a resource, and this document does not invent one. A status code is the outcome the specification declares — 202 for a branch that was taken, 422 for a refusal the input decides, 502 for a refusal decided outside the request — and the `outcome` property of every response body names the branch. This component publishes `ConfigChanged`, `InstanceAnswered`, `InstancePurged`, `InstanceReconciled`, `InstanceRestarted`, `InstanceRolledBack`, `InstanceStarted`, `InstanceStopped`, `InstanceUnreachable`, `InstanceUpgrading`, `OperatorJoined`, `OperatorLeft`, `BoxClosed`, `BoxOpened`, `BoxRefused`, `SecretPut`, `SecretsResolved`, `StoreMigrated`, `TokenContributed`, `TokenLeased`, `TokenLimited`, `TokenReleased` and `TokenWithdrawn` to consumers through the event transport; an event a branch emits that is not among them stays inside the component. The `published` property of every response body lists every event its branch emitted, in the order it emits them, published or not.

The specification declares who may invoke what (`x-ess-may-invoke` on each operation), so every command is sent as a declared actor. How a request proves which actor it is belongs to the realization, which authenticates it and hands the surface the caller; nothing in the request itself names one. The grant is checked before the command runs, and a request authenticated as no actor, or as one without the grant, is answered 403 with one standard refusal, the same for every command: `{"refused": "not granted", "actor": <name or null>}`. A 403 a declared branch answers carries `outcome` and the declared `error` instead, so a client tells the two apart by the members present. A command no declared actor may invoke is refused to every caller. A view an actor's grant names is read-checked the same way (`x-ess-may-read` on its operation): a request authenticated as no actor, or as one the grant does not name, is answered 403 with the same standard refusal before the view is read. A view no grant names is open, and any caller may read what it publishes.

This component declares `reached_by: network`, so its callers are not deployed with it and this contract is the surface they reach it through. That declaration is also why the views its domains declare have paths here: a GET under `views` per projection, answering every row it holds. There is no page size, no cursor, no ordering and no filter parameter, because the specification states none — a view's filter is part of the projection, not of the request. A view that declares `params:` is the exception: each is a query parameter, described on its operation, and a view that declares `paging:` takes its page and size there.

tags.name: config
tags.description: The one file conductord reconciles from, `conductor.config/2`, read from `--config`, else the `conductor-config` setting, else ~/.b10x/conductor/conductor.yaml (story:config-file; docs/design/architecture-next.md § 9). It holds the `daemon` section (its port, TLS listener, reconcile cadence, the one store URL, the secrets source, the dashboard's served path and its operators), `globals` (the defaults every instance starts from) and `instances[]`. An instance is one organization conductor runs: its placement, where its repositories come from, where their checkouts are, where conductor keeps its records, state and cache, which kind and model each role runs on, its cadence, thresholds, reports, and who decides each decision class; every key an instance or a role writes overrides the global one. Precedence is role over instance over global (`Level`), and `EffectiveSettings` shows every key with its effective value and the level it came from. These types hold the effective config, after defaults; the file may leave out every key of an instance but its name, its sources and its checkouts. No field takes a secret: the file names one as `secret:<name>` (`conductor.secret.SecretName`). The config is desired state and is not kept in the store (§ 8); every change through `PutConfig` is validated, written, committed with its actor and reason, recorded as `ConfigChanged` and reconciled. A `conductor.config/1` file is read once by `conductor config migrate`.

tags.name: instance
tags.description: The instances conductord reconciles (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 4): desired state from the config (name, placement, roles, settings), actual state from what runs (state, binary version, last seen, box), and one `Reconciliation` record per action the daemon takes (start, stop, restart, upgrade, nothing). Replaces the registry types of `conductor.host`.

tags.name: operator
tags.description: Who acts on conductor, told apart by kind (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 3 "Actors", § 5.3, decisions 9, 11, 12 and 14). An `Actor` is a kind and the fields of that kind: `Human`, an operator (an Identity principal with grants); `Agent`, a program the runtime started in a role of an instance; `Daemon`, conductord or an instance runtime acting on its own account. Every command in every domain carries its `actor`; every event and every record derived from one carries the same; a grant belongs to a human actor only, and a command that needs one refuses every other kind by name, as a predicate over `actor.kind`. The instance cluster has several operators; an operator joins an instance and leaves it; the records projection writes an actor as `human:<name>`, `agent:<instance>/<role>/<name>` or `daemon`.

tags.name: placement
tags.description: Where an instance runs: a Substrate box, opened by a substrate daemon on this host or by a remote one named by URL with a bearer, through one of the adapters `systemd`, `linux` (bubblewrap), `oci` or `pod` (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 6, decision 3). A placement carries the box's profile: read-only roots, the writable workspace, limits, egress and the secret slots. Conductor implements no sandbox: conductord asks substrate to open the box with the profile, and a refusal is recorded as a box refusal with substrate's own reason, by name, and nothing falls back (ADR 0109, quoted in § 6). Replaces `confinement.provider`, `confinement.mode` and the systemd provider's places (§ 3).

tags.name: secret
tags.description: The config names secrets and never holds them (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 9, decision 6): a `secret:<name>` is resolved by the daemon through the `secrets` crates, the OS keychain on a workstation and the Secrets service where conductord is deployed, and handed to a box as a sealed slot at box open (§ 6). The API lists names and sources, never values. The specification holds no secret value anywhere: no type, field, input, event, error or view below carries one.

tags.name: store
tags.description:
One shared database per deployment (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 8, decision 13), opened through Eventlog's port: `sqlite` for a deployment that is one host, `postgres` for everything else. `daemon.store` names the one URL; the daemon hands it to every instance runtime it starts; every event names its instance; every UI and every operator reads the same records. No copy per instance, no sync, no restore. Today's eventlog tree is read once by the migration (`conductor store migrate`) and not opened again.
No command opens the store: § 2 and § 8 say the daemon opens it at start and hands its URL to every runtime, and neither lists that opening among the records the store keeps (decisions, dispatches, readings, findings, charters, hand-offs, snapshots, config changes, reconciliations). The `Store` row is the deployment's, not a command's.

tags.name: token
tags.description: The token pool of an instance (design docs/design/architecture-next.md § 5.3, decisions 10 and 11): an engineer who joins an instance contributes their Claude token; the pool is a set of secrets, each with its owner, its seat and its state (`ok`, or `limited until <time>`); values never leave the secrets source except as a sealed slot. The `claude-code` kind leases one token per agent start, resumes an agent on another token after a usage-limit stop, and names the token's owner on every agent record. A controller started for Remote Control on a named owner's token appears in that owner's Claude app.
